steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Goal setting: The process of identifying something you want to achieve and establishing measurable objectives and timeframes to work towards it. Goal setting provides direction, motivation and focus for performers. | Exam Tip: Performance goals are generally more effective because they are within the performer's control. Even if you lose a match, you can still achieve a performance goal. This maintains motivation. Outcome goals are useful for long-term ambition but should be supported by performance goals. | Goal Achievement Cycle: Set goal → Work towards it → Evaluate progress → Adjust if needed → Achieve goal → Set new goal. This cycle ensures continuous improvement and prevents complacency after achieving a goal. | PE Exam Tips — Goal Setting and SMART Targets: 1. For Goal Setting and S

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the difference between a performance goal and an outcome goal, using a sporting example. | What does each letter in SMART stand for? Explain why each element is important. | Rewrite this non-SMART goal as a SMART goal: "I want to be a better runner."
